header.userPrompt:
Add a button to the bank statement viewer that manually (re)generates the AI category/merchant suggestions for that statement.

CONTEXT (already shipped in PR #7, reuse it — do not duplicate logic):
- bank_statement has a nullable `ai_suggestions JSONB` column holding AiSuggestions { status: enum Pending/Done/Failed (stored as its string name), model, rows:[{rowId, categoryId?, merchantId?}] }.
- A background job `BackgroundJobPayload.ResolveStatementSuggestions(bankStatementId)` + its handler already compute suggestions for the rows no import rule matches (category, then merchant-from-category, via Nova), and write all rows atomically, flipping status to Done/Failed. It is currently enqueued only at draft confirm.
- GetBankStatement.Response already returns aiSuggestions, and the statement view already shows per-row suggestions and polls while status is Pending.

GOAL: let the user trigger that same job on demand for an EXISTING statement from the statement viewer UI. For a statement that already has suggestions, this RECOMPUTES them (overwrite). For an old statement that never had any (ai_suggestions is null), this generates them.

BUILD:

1. Shared API (lib/api/shared): a new authenticated endpoint to trigger regeneration for one statement, e.g. POST `/bank-statements/{id}/ai-suggestions`, following the existing bank-statement endpoint conventions. Response can be empty/accepted or echo the new status.

2. Backend: a controller wiring + a thin action (e.g. RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction) that:
   - verifies the statement belongs to the authenticated user (user-scoped; fail if not found),
   - sets bank_statement.ai_suggestions to status Pending (reuse the existing AiSuggestions model/enum; existing rows may be cleared or left until the job overwrites them — but status MUST become Pending so the UI shows the in-progress state),
   - enqueues the EXISTING ResolveStatementSuggestions background job for that bankStatementId.
   Reuse the existing job handler unchanged — recompute is just re-enqueue + atomic overwrite. Do NOT re-implement suggestion logic.

3. Frontend: on the page that displays a confirmed statement's rows and its AI suggestions (the same page touched in PR #7), add a button, e.g. "Regenerate AI suggestions", that calls the new endpoint. After the call, rely on the EXISTING Pending-status polling to refresh the suggestions — do not build a second polling mechanism. Disable the button (and/or show a spinner) while status is Pending so it can't be double-triggered. The button lives on an existing, already-reachable page.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Reuse the PR #7 job, handler, model, and polling; this feature is a trigger + button only.
- Keep changes surgical; do not restyle or refactor unrelated UI; do not touch draft->confirm.
- User-scoped DB access; fail loud on a missing/foreign statement; no silent defaults.
- Follow docs/guide conventions. Add/adjust tests for: the action (ownership check, sets status Pending, enqueues the job) and the endpoint; a web test for the button if conventions require.

resultJson.description:
Add a way for the user to (re)generate AI category and merchant suggestions for an existing confirmed bank statement, from the statement review page. PR #7 already does the hard part. A `ResolveStatementSuggestions` background job computes suggestions for rows that no import rule matches and writes them in one atomic `setAiSuggestions` call, ending as Done or Failed. `GetBankStatement.Response.aiSuggestions` returns the result, and `BankStatementReviewPage` shows per-row suggestions and polls while they are missing or Pending. Today the job is only enqueued when a draft is confirmed. Statements confirmed before PR #7 therefore have `ai_suggestions = NULL` forever, and suggestions that already exist can never be recomputed (for example after the user adds categories or merchants).

This epic adds a trigger and nothing else. A new authenticated endpoint, `POST /bank-statements/{bankStatementId}/ai-suggestions`, does two things in one DB transaction: it overwrites the statement's `ai_suggestions` with `AiSuggestions(Pending, <configured model id>, Nil)`, and it enqueues the existing `ResolveStatementSuggestions(bankStatementId)` job. The update is scoped by `WHERE user_id`, so a missing or foreign statement fails with "Bank statement not found" and no job is created. The existing job handler then recomputes and overwrites the suggestions unchanged. The response echoes the new Pending `AiSuggestions`.

On the frontend, a "Regenerate AI suggestions" button in the review page header calls the endpoint. It puts the returned Pending value into page state and resets the existing poll-attempt counter, so the existing poll loop restarts and picks up Done or Failed. The button is disabled while a request is in flight or while the status is Pending. There is no new polling mechanism, and the suggestion logic, the job handler and draft confirm are not changed.

tasks.title: Repository: atomically set AI suggestions to Pending and enqueue the suggestions job
tasks.description:
Add a method to `BankStatementRepository` (server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepository.scala), for example:
`def requestAiSuggestions(id: UUID, userId: UUID, pending: AiSuggestions, job: BackgroundJobData.Create, updatedAt: Instant): Future[Unit] = Future { database.withTransaction { implicit conn => BankStatementDAO.setAiSuggestions(id, userId, pending, updatedAt); BackgroundJobDAO.create(job) } }`

- Reuse the existing `BankStatementDAO.setAiSuggestions`. It is user-scoped and throws `RuntimeException("Bank statement not found")` when 0 rows are updated. Because it runs first in the transaction, a missing or foreign statement rolls back and no job row is created.
- Do not add new SQL or a new DAO method.

Tests go in server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/BankStatementRepositorySpec.scala, in a new `"requestAiSuggestions" should { ... }` block (RULE-TE-001: no class name in the subject):
- (a) It stores the given Pending suggestions. Check via `find(id, userId).aiSuggestions` = `Some(pending)`. It also overwrites a previously stored Done value: call `setAiSuggestions` with Done first.
- (b) It enqueues exactly one `ResolveStatementSuggestions` job whose payload is `{"bankStatementId": id}`. Read `background_jobs` via raw SQL, like the existing `createConfirmedStatement` "enqueue the given job" test does.
- (c) For a statement owned by another user it fails with a message containing "Bank statement not found", leaves the owner's `aiSuggestions` unchanged (None), and inserts no `background_jobs` row.

Build the job with `BackgroundJobData.Create(id = UUID.randomUUID(), type = BackgroundJobType.ResolveStatementSuggestions, payload = BackgroundJobPayload.ResolveStatementSuggestions(stmtId), status = BackgroundJobStatus.Pending, executeAt = now, createdAt = now, updatedAt = now)`.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"`.

tasks.title: Shared endpoint + RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction + controller wiring, with controller tests
tasks.description:
1. Shared model: new file lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/bankstatements/RegenerateAiSuggestions.scala, in the same style as IgnoreRow.scala and DeleteBankStatement.scala: `object RegenerateAiSuggestions { case class Response(aiSuggestions: AiSuggestions); implicit val responseFormat: Format[Response] = Json.format[Response]; implicit val responseSchema: Schema[Response] = Schema.derived[Response].name(Schema.SName("RegenerateAiSuggestionsResponse")) }`. Import `sttp.tapir.generic.auto.*` if derivation needs it; `AiSuggestions` already has a format and a lazy schema.

2. Endpoint: in lib/api/shared/.../endpoints/BankStatementsEndpoints.scala add `def regenerateAiSuggestions(implicit authHandler: ServerRequest => Future[UUID]): Endpoint[Unit, (UUID, Future[UUID]), ErrorResponse, RegenerateAiSuggestions.Response, Any] = baseEndpoint.post.in(path[UUID]("bankStatementId") / "ai-suggestions").in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[RegenerateAiSuggestions.Response]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest)).summary("(Re)generate the AI category/merchant suggestions for a bank statement")`. Add it to `routes`.

3. ApiClient: in lib/api/shared/.../ApiClient.scala add `def regenerateBankStatementAiSuggestions(bankStatementId: UUID): Future[RegenerateAiSuggestions.Response] = handleRequest(BankStatementsEndpoints.regenerateAiSuggestions, (bankStatementId, dummyUserId))` next to `getBankStatement`.

4. Action: new server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction.scala: `class RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction @Inject() (bankStatementRepository: BankStatementRepository, bedrockConfig: BedrockConfig)(implicit ec: ExecutionContext, clock: Clock)`. `apply(bankStatementId: UUID, userId: UUID): Future[RegenerateAiSuggestions.Response]`:
   - `now = clock.instant()`
   - `pending = AiSuggestions(AiSuggestionsStatus.Pending, bedrockConfig.suggestionsModelId, Nil)`
   - `job = BackgroundJobData.Create(...ResolveStatementSuggestions(bankStatementId), executeAt = now...)`, as in ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction.
   - `bankStatementRepository.requestAiSuggestions(bankStatementId, userId, pending, job, now)`
   - Log at info with the statement id and job id, then return `Response(pending)`.
   - The flat for-comprehension has no inline conditionals (RULE-BE-009); the ownership check is in the repository.

5. Controller: in server/src/main/scala/controllers/BankStatementsController.scala, inject `regenerateAiSuggestionsAction: RegenerateAiSuggestionsAction`. Add `private def regenerateAiSuggestions(bankStatementId: UUID, userIdF: Future[UUID]) = handleRequest { logger.info(s"Regenerate AI suggestions: stmt=$bankStatementId"); for { userId <- userIdF; response <- regenerateAiSuggestionsAction(bankStatementId, userId) } yield Right(response) }` and add `BankStatementsEndpoints.regenerateAiSuggestions.serverLogic(regenerateAiSuggestions)` to `routes`.

6. Tests: in server/src/test/scala/controllers/BankStatementsControllerSpec.scala, add a `"POST /bank-statements/:id/ai-suggestions"` block. Actions are tested through controller specs (RULE-TE-005).
   - (a) Returns `aiSuggestions.status == Pending` with `rows == Nil` for a fresh statement (aiSuggestions None).
   - (b) Overwrites existing Done suggestions: seed them with `app.injector.instanceOf[BankStatementRepository].setAiSuggestions(...)`, as the existing "return the stored AI suggestions" test does. The response is Pending.
   - (c) Enqueues a `ResolveStatementSuggestions` job for the statement. Count rows with raw SQL as in BankStatementDraftControllerSpec "enqueue a ResolveStatementSuggestions job" (`UPPER(type) = BackgroundJobType.ResolveStatementSuggestions.entryName AND payload ->> 'bankStatementId' = stmtId`). The count goes from 1 to 2, because `createBankStatementWithRows` already seeds one far-future job.
   - (d) A second user (`buildClient()` + `createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)(using executionContext, client2)`) gets `expectError == "Bank statement not found"`, and the job count stays 1.
   - (e) A random UUID gets "Bank statement not found".
   - Do not assert that the stored status stays Pending in this spec: the live executor (polling every 10s, starting about 1 min after app start, with MockBedrockClient) may flip it to Done. The repository spec covers the stored Pending value deterministically.

Verify with `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Frontend: "Regenerate AI suggestions" button on BankStatementReviewPage reusing the existing poll
tasks.description:
File: web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala. This page is already reachable from the statement list, so no router change is needed.

1. Add a pure companion helper next to `suggestionsPending`, for example `def canRegenerateSuggestions(ai: Option[AiSuggestions]): Boolean = !ai.exists(_.status == AiSuggestionsStatus.Pending)`.
   - NULL (never generated), Done and Failed are all regeneratable.
   - Do not reuse `suggestionsPending` for this: it treats None as pending, which would disable the button for old statements, the main use case.

2. Add state `val (regeneratingSuggestions, setRegeneratingSuggestions) = Hooks.useState(false)`, and a handler `handleRegenerateSuggestions(stmtId: UUID)`:
   - `setRegeneratingSuggestions(true)`, then call `props.ctx.api.client.regenerateBankStatementAiSuggestions(stmtId).onComplete` (RULE-FE-008).
   - On Success(resp): `setError("")`; `setStatement(cur => cur.map(_.copy(aiSuggestions = Some(resp.aiSuggestions))))`; `setSuggestionsPollAttempts(0)`; `setRegeneratingSuggestions(false)`; `showToast("Regenerating AI suggestions…")`.
   - On Failure(ex): `setError(ex.getMessage)`; `setRegeneratingSuggestions(false)`.
   - The existing poll effect is keyed on `s"$stmtId:$pollingSuggestions"`, so a Done/Failed → Pending change restarts the interval automatically. Resetting the attempts counter re-opens the 20×3s window after an earlier cap expired, and extends it if a NULL statement is still polling.
   - Do NOT add another interval or effect. Do not use setTimeout tricks.

3. Add the button in the header row, next to the existing "Auto-reconcile" button, in the same style: `mui.Button.normal()("Regenerate AI suggestions").size("small").variant("outlined").disabled(regeneratingSuggestions || !canRegenerateSuggestions(stmt.aiSuggestions)).onClick(_ => handleRegenerateSuggestions(stmt.id))`. Optionally show `mui.CircularProgress().size(14)` or change the label to "Regenerating…" while disabled due to Pending. Do not restyle anything else.

4. Tests: add a `"canRegenerateSuggestions"` block to web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPageSpec.scala, mirroring the existing `suggestionsPending` tests: true for None, Done and Failed; false for Pending. No DOM test (RULE-TE-010).

Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules
- `lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/`: Tapir endpoints (`endpoints/BankStatementsEndpoints.scala`), request/response models (`models/bankstatements/*`), and the shared `ApiClient.scala`, which is used by the web app (`props.ctx.api.client`) and by the controller tests.
- `server/`: Play backend. Call direction is controllers → actions → repositories → DAOs (docs/guide/backend.md). Actions never call other actions. Repositories wrap each operation in one `Future { database.withTransaction/withConnection { ... } }` and decide atomicity. DAOs hold the raw Anorm SQL.
- `web/`: Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5. The statement viewer is `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankStatementReviewPage.scala` (route `/bank-statements/:stmtId`, already linked from the statements list).

## Existing pieces from PR #7 (reuse, do not change)
- `AiSuggestions(status: AiSuggestionsStatus, model: String, rows: List[AiSuggestions.RowSuggestion])` in lib/api/shared/.../models/bankstatements/AiSuggestions.scala. It has a Play JSON `Format` and a lazy Tapir `Schema`. `AiSuggestionsStatus` is an enumeratum enum (Pending/Done/Failed); `model` is a required String.
- `GetBankStatement.Response.aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions]`. None means never computed: statements confirmed before PR #7 and statements seeded in tests.
- `BankStatementDAO.setAiSuggestions(id, userId, suggestions, updatedAt)(implicit conn)` (server/.../repositories/daos/BankStatementDAO.scala). It is user-scoped (`WHERE id AND user_id`) and throws `RuntimeException("Bank statement not found")` if 0 rows are updated. `BankStatementRepository.setAiSuggestions` wraps it in `withConnection`.
- `BackgroundJobDAO.create(job: BackgroundJobData.Create)(implicit conn)` (server/.../repositories/daos/BackgroundJobDAO.scala), already imported in BankStatementRepository.
- Job: `BackgroundJobType.ResolveStatementSuggestions` + `BackgroundJobPayload.ResolveStatementSuggestions(bankStatementId: UUID)` (server/.../models/jobs/). Example construction is in `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction` (server/.../actions/bankstatements/), which you must not modify: `BackgroundJobData.Create(id = UUID.randomUUID(), \`type\` = ..., payload = ..., status = BackgroundJobStatus.Pending, executeAt = now, createdAt = now, updatedAt = now)`.
- Handler: `ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.apply(bankStatementId)` (server/.../actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala). It uses `bankStatementRepository.findInternal`, computes suggestions, and stores Done (or Failed and re-raises) with one `setAiSuggestions`. Its model id comes from the injectable `BedrockConfig.suggestionsModelId` (server/.../config/BedrockConfig.scala). Use the same value for the Pending placeholder's `model`. It is dispatched by `BackgroundJobsExecutorTask`.
- Executor timing: the first run is `backgroundJobsExecutorTask.interval` (1 minute) after app start. After that, `StreamPendingBackgroundJobsForeverAction` re-polls pending jobs every 10s. In controller tests the live executor runs with `MockBedrockClient`, which returns no suggestions, so a newly enqueued job may flip the status to Done during a long test. Don't assert a stored Pending in controller specs.

## Controller/endpoint conventions
- Endpoints: `baseEndpoint.post.in(path[UUID]("bankStatementId") / "...").in(userAuth).out(jsonBody[X.Response]).errorOut(oneOf(HttpErrors.badRequest)).summary(...)`, and every endpoint is listed in `routes`. Response models are `object X { case class Response(...); implicit val responseFormat = Json.format[Response]; implicit val responseSchema = Schema.derived[Response].name(Schema.SName("XResponse")) }`. See IgnoreRow.scala and DeleteBankStatement.scala.
- ApiClient methods: `def foo(id: UUID): Future[X.Response] = handleRequest(BankStatementsEndpoints.foo, (id, dummyUserId))`.
- `controllers.BankStatementsController`: each handler is `handleRequest { logger.info(...); for { userId <- userIdF; response <- action(...) } yield Right(response) }`, plus `Endpoint.serverLogic(handler)` in `routes`. Actions are injected via the constructor.
- Errors: throw a `RuntimeException` with a human-readable message. `handleRequest` turns it into `ErrorResponse(message)`, and tests read it via `.expectError`. A missing or foreign statement must fail loudly with "Bank statement not found" (existing tests assert this exact string). Never use silent defaults.

## Testing conventions (docs/guide/testing.md)
- Repository specs extend `RepositorySpec with RepositoryUtils` and use `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }`, `createUser()`, `createBankStatement(userId)`, and `repositories.bankStatements` / `repositories.database`. Raw SQL reads of `background_jobs` are acceptable; see the `createConfirmedStatement` test in BankStatementRepositorySpec. Users for other-user tests: `createUser(email = Email.trusted("a@test.com"))`.
- Controller specs (`BankStatementsControllerSpec`) use `withApiClient { implicit client => createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator).futureValue; val (stmtId, rowId) = setupStmtWithRow() ... }`. `createBankStatementWithRows` (PlayPostgresSpec) already enqueues ONE far-future `ResolveStatementSuggestions` job per statement, so account for it when counting. Second user: `val client2 = buildClient(); createVerifyLoginUser(tokenGenerator)(using executionContext, client2).futureValue`. Job-count SQL example is in BankStatementDraftControllerSpec: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM background_jobs WHERE UPPER(type) = ${BackgroundJobType.ResolveStatementSuggestions.entryName} AND payload ->> 'bankStatementId' = ${stmtId.toString}`, run via `app.injector.instanceOf[Database].withConnection`.
- Actions are not unit-tested directly; controller specs cover them.
- `should` subjects never repeat the class name.
- Frontend: no DOM tests unless guarding a known crash (RULE-TE-010). Extract pure functions on the page's companion object and test them in `BankStatementReviewPageSpec` (AnyWordSpec + `mustBe`), like the existing `suggestionsPending` tests.
- Verify with targeted runs only: `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementRepositorySpec"`, `sbt "testOnly *BankStatementsControllerSpec"`, `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewPageSpec"`, and `CI=true sbt Test/compile` (`-Werror`: unused imports fail). Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.

## Frontend specifics (BankStatementReviewPage)
- State: `statement: Option[GetBankStatement.Response]` via `setStatement`; `error`/`setError`; `showToast(msg)`.
- Poll: `suggestionsPollAttempts`/`setSuggestionsPollAttempts` (cap `SuggestionsPollMaxAttempts = 20`, every 3000 ms). `pollingSuggestions = statement.exists(s => suggestionsPending(s.aiSuggestions)) && attempts < cap`. The effect is keyed on `s"$stmtId:$pollingSuggestions"` and only copies `aiSuggestions` from each refetch. Restarting it means making `pollingSuggestions` true: set aiSuggestions to Some(Pending) and reset the attempts to 0.
- `suggestionsPending(None) == true` by design, so don't use it to gate the button.
- `matchCell` already shows "suggesting…" for unmatched debit rows while polling. `BankRowCreateExpenseForm` reads `stmt.aiSuggestions.flatMap(_.rows.find(_.rowId == row.id))`, so clearing rows to Nil while Pending is safe.
- Header buttons: `mui.Button.normal()("Auto-reconcile").size("small").variant("outlined").onClick(...)`. Use API calls with `.onComplete` (RULE-FE-008). No `js.Dynamic`/`asInstanceOf` in the page (RULE-FE-014). Object-level `val`s may only be plain style literals (RULE-FE-002).

## Non-obvious notes
- Do the Pending write and the job insert in one repository transaction, with `setAiSuggestions` first, so its not-found throw rolls back and no orphan job is created. This also serves as the ownership check, so the action needs no separate find or inline `if`.
- The server does not dedupe concurrent regenerations. Two jobs simply both overwrite the value, and the UI disable prevents double triggers. Don't add a server-side guard unless asked.
- Don't touch `ConfirmBankStatementDraftAction`, `ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction`, `StatementSuggestionsService`, or `BackgroundJobPayload`.

reason.text: Out of scope. The plan for this task decided against a server-side guard: "The server does not dedupe concurrent regenerations ... Don't add a server-side guard unless asked." A reviewer can't override that, so the user has to decide whether to add one. The suggested guard would also clash with the UI as written. The page stops polling and re-enables the button after 20 × 3000 ms = 60 s (BankStatementReviewPage.scala:84-85, 175). A 2-minute Pending timeout would therefore reject the legitimate retry the UI allows. Picking the timeout, choosing between a per-user rate limit and status-based rejection, and handling a Pending status left stuck by a crashed job all need a product decision. Abuse is also limited: the endpoint is authenticated and user-scoped, so only an account holder can trigger jobs, and only for their own statements. Recommend a follow-up task for rate limiting the paid suggestions jobs.

The full suite passed on the first run, so I didn't change any code. I ran `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` and it exited with code 0 after about 18 minutes.

| Module | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| Shared modules | 36 + 24 (each ran twice) | 0 |
| Web | 166 | 0 |
| Server | 693 | 0 |

- **Node version:** the default Node here, v16.7.0, rejects `--openssl-legacy-provider` in `NODE_OPTIONS`. I used Node v24.15.0 from nvm instead, which matches `.nvmrc` and CI (`node-version: '24'`).
- **Postgres:** Docker was available, so the testcontainers Postgres started on its own.
- **`[error]` lines in the log:** none are test failures. Two are yarn warnings (one about a peer dependency). The other three come from tests that deliberately exercise failure paths, such as a model returning invalid JSON.

The only change in the working tree is `.orca/runs/87c1d14ae277.progress.json`, which was already modified before this run.
